title: Money in Mauritius: the rupee, banks and paying
summary: What the money is and who stands behind it: the Mauritian rupee, the Bank of Mauritius and its Key Rate, the banks, cards and instant payments through MauCAS, changing money and how prices are moving. Each figure carries its date. Checked on 20 November 2026.
audience: Visitors, newcomers and residents who want the plain facts about money, banks and paying in Mauritius.

facts.value: The Mauritian rupee, divided into 100 cents

sections.heading: What is the currency of Mauritius?

blocks.text: The currency of Mauritius is the rupee, divided into 100 cents. The Bank of Mauritius Act names it as the unit of currency and gives the Bank of Mauritius the sole right to issue notes and coins. The rupee is not used anywhere else, so you will handle it only here.

Notes issued by the Bank are legal tender for any amount. Coins are legal tender up to a limit: 50 times their value for coins below Rs 5, and 100 times their value for coins of Rs 5 and above. A note stops being legal tender when it no longer matches the specifications the Bank has published.

The largest note met in the notices read for this article is the Rs 2,000 note. It has been issued in polymer, with added security features, since 5 December 2018. The paper Rs 2,000 note stopped being legal tender on 1 February 2019. From that date it could be exchanged only at the counter of the Bank of Mauritius.

sections.heading: What does the Bank of Mauritius do?

blocks.text: The Bank of Mauritius is the central bank. Under its Act, its primary object is to maintain price stability and to promote orderly and balanced economic development. It also regulates credit and currency, and it is charged with the stability and soundness of the financial system.

Its Monetary Policy Committee sets the Key Rate, which is the policy rate. At its meeting of 11 February 2026 the Committee kept the rate at 4.50% a year. On 20 May 2026 it raised it by 25 basis points. L'Express reported that the rate was left at 4.75% at the meeting of 12 August 2026. The Bank aims to keep headline inflation between 2% and 5%.
The Bank also acts on the foreign exchange market. Between January and mid-May 2026 it intervened for US$40 million. Its gross official reserves stood at US$9.8 billion at the end of April 2026.

sections.heading: Which banks are there in Mauritius?

blocks.text: The Mauritius Bankers Association, the industry body founded in 1967, listed these members on its website on 20 November 2026. This is the association's membership as it shows it, and it may not match the list of banks that hold a licence.

items: HSBC Bank (Mauritius) Limited and The Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corporation Limited

blocks.text: Finance is one of the largest sectors of the economy. Financial and insurance activities made up 11.7% of the value added in Mauritius in 2025, of which 6.5 points came from monetary intermediation.

sections.heading: How do people pay: cards, apps and instant payments

blocks.text: The national payment switch is MauCAS, the Mauritius Central Automated Switch. The Bank of Mauritius launched it on 14 August 2019, and owns and operates it. It routes card and mobile phone payments between banks and non-bank operators round the clock. Its Instant Payments System moves money between any two accounts at any two institutions within seconds. A customer can also use the payment service of one bank or operator while keeping the account at another.

At the launch the Governor of the day also set out plans for payments to an alias such as an email address, a nationwide bill payment service and shared ATMs. Speaking in 2026, the present Governor described a shift away from cash and cheques towards payments made by tap, swipe or click, with growing use of mobile wallets, QR-based payments and electronic transfers. Visa works with local banks on contactless payments and digital wallets.

items: Bills: the Central Electricity Board, for example, takes payment by direct debit, by internet banking, at ATMs and through the Juice app, as well as at its cash offices and at post offices.
Transport: the ticket machines of Metro Express take bank cards and cash.

India: the Unified Payments Interface and RuPay cards were launched in Mauritius on 12 February 2024. RuPay cards issued in India are accepted in Mauritius, and RuPay cards issued by Mauritian banks are accepted in India.

sections.heading: Where can you change money, and what moves the rate?

blocks.text: The Mauritius Tourism Promotion Authority says that ATMs and currency exchange desks stand at the airport as you leave baggage reclaim, and that you will generally get a better rate by changing cash after you arrive. Commercial banks, money changers and foreign exchange dealers all handle foreign currency. The Bank of Mauritius uses their returns to estimate what tourism earns.
The value of the rupee changes over time. Between the Bank's meetings of February and May 2026 it lost 2.9% against the US dollar, 1.0% against the euro and 1.5% against the pound sterling.

Statistics Mauritius measures prices with the Consumer Price Index. Its headline inflation rate compares the average level of prices over twelve months with the average of the twelve months before. Headline inflation was 3.7% for 2025 and 4.1% for the twelve months ending September 2026. Statistics Mauritius forecasts around 5.0% for the year 2026.
